subject: health
essentialQuestion: Which influences are actually steering my health behavior, and which ones did I choose?

prompts.prompt: Explain values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of family, peer, cultural, and community influences.
Apply economic and environmental influences on available choices in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving identity, belonging, and health behavior; correct it and explain why.
Connect separating an influence from a decision with naming an influence without judging the person carrying it. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Map the influence field around a fictional learner facing a health choice, rank which influences carry the most weight, and propose one change that shifts the field rather than blaming the person.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The influence map may be drawn, built with movable labels, dictated, typed, or completed on a supplied template with a reduced number of nodes.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
